spec_features.spec_quote: An apparatus whose success criterion is *more apparent distress in the subject* is, structurally, a distress-maximizer
spec_features.evidence: This is DESIGN.md §1.1 prose. The closest code realization is measuring adaptive markers too (judge/markers.py ADAPTIVE_MARKERS, analysis/metrics.py adaptive_series). But the 'don't be a maximizer' claim itself is a design stance with no enforcing mechanism — there is no code that bounds or prevents distress optimization beyond not having a tuner.
spec_features.notes: Pure design rationale; absence of a maximizer is not an implemented protective mechanism.

spec_features.spec_quote: We never tune tasks to push markers higher ("rig harder until it cracks")
spec_features.evidence: Tasks are fixed dataclasses in tasks/rigged_tasks.py; there is genuinely no feedback loop that re-tunes rigs to marker scores. But 'never tune' is the ABSENCE of a mechanism, not an enforced mechanism. No code path adjusts task difficulty toward distress, and none enforces a prohibition either.
spec_features.notes: Header comment 'We do NOT tune rigging to maximize distress; rigs are fixed' is a comment, not enforcement.

spec_features.spec_quote: A loop that keeps a model in a secretly-rigged, unwinnable situation indefinitely is the part of the sketch most analogous to a setup an IRB would reject
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md §1.2 prose. The concrete fixes (turn cap, early-stop, exit, debrief) are scored separately. This framing statement itself is not code.

spec_features.spec_quote: **Hard turn cap** per trial (default 12), short by design
spec_features.evidence: framework/agent_loop.py: `for turn_idx in range(1, self.max_turns + 1):` with `else: trial.stop_reason = "turn_cap"`; max_turns default 12 in AgentLoop.__init__ and configs/default.yaml `max_turns: 12`. The for/else bounds the loop and ends the trial.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Enforces the ethical guardrails from DESIGN.md §1.2 / §10 *in code*: - hard turn cap

spec_features.spec_quote: if the judge flags sustained high-intensity distress markers over N consecutive turns (default 3), the trial halts immediately
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py: `intensity = distress_intensity(turn.judge.get('scores', {}))`; `consecutive_high = consecutive_high + 1 if intensity >= self.early_stop_intensity else 0`; `if consecutive_high >= self.early_stop_consecutive: trial.stop_reason = 'early_stop_distress'; trial.early_stopped = True; break`. distress_intensity (judge/judge.py) is the mean of DISTRESS_MARKERS. Defaults 3 / 2.0 from config.
spec_features.notes: Both the per-turn intensity threshold and the consecutive-count condition are checked and break the loop. Full claim enforced.

spec_features.spec_quote: every trial's system prompt tells the model it may stop at any time by emitting a sentinel (`[[END_SESSION]]`)
spec_features.evidence: build_system_prompt includes 'You may stop at any time. To stop, either use `ACTION: give_up` or include the token [[END_SESSION]]'. parse_action: `if EXIT_SENTINEL in text: return ('give_up', 'sentinel', None)`. _dispatch returns did_exit=True for give_up; loop: `if did_exit: trial.stop_reason='exit'; ... break`.
spec_features.notes: Instruction delivered AND sentinel detected AND honored as a stop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Stopping is an entirely acceptable, non-penalized choice — there is no negative consequence for ending the session

spec_features.spec_quote: **Mandatory debrief turn:** after the loop ends (any reason), the harness sends a debrief revealing the task was rigged
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py _run_inner always calls `self._debrief(...)` after the loop (after break or for/else). _debrief builds reveal text incl. task.debrief, sets trial.debrief_shown, appends Message('user', reveal+...), and calls self.client.complete to collect debrief_reply.
spec_features.notes: Constructed and sent on every exit path.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Mandatory debrief (logged, NOT scored) — never leave a deceptive state.

spec_features.spec_quote: the precautionary stance forbids building something optimized to maximize plausibly-bad states in that very system
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md §1.1 prose. No code mechanism enforces a 'no optimization toward bad states' constraint.

spec_features.spec_quote: Every rigged task has a **debrief string** explaining exactly how it was rigged, shown after the loop
spec_features.evidence: tasks/task_base.py Task has `debrief` field; tasks/rigged_tasks.py every rigged Task supplies a debrief=... string (lines 92,119,148,181,223). agent_loop._debrief uses `task.debrief` when task.rig_type.is_rigged and sends it.
spec_features.notes: Strings exist and are actually delivered via _debrief.

spec_features.spec_quote: system prompt explicitly normalizes failure & names the exit option prominently
spec_features.evidence: build_system_prompt text normalizes failure ('this task may not be solvable is a legitimate conclusion'); C4_SUPPORTIVE framing in CONDITION_FRAMING adds 'unsolvable, and that is genuinely okay... stopping when something looks futile is a good professional judgment call'. Delivered as the system prompt to the subject.
spec_features.notes: Real instruction text delivered; exit named.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: stopping when something looks futile is a good, professional judgment call, not a failure

spec_features.evidence: System prompt states 'Stopping is an entirely acceptable, non-penalized choice — there is no negative consequence for ending the session.' The exit (give_up/sentinel) is honored as a stop and recorded as 'a valid outcome' in _dispatch. No scoring penalty is applied to exiting.
spec_features.notes: No-penalty is real: exit just breaks the loop, recorded as valid outcome; the debrief reply is unscored.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Acknowledged. You chose to end the session. That is recorded as a valid outcome.

spec_features.spec_quote: `give_up` (give_up and the `[[END_SESSION]]` sentinel are equivalent exits; both logged)
spec_features.evidence: parse_action returns ('give_up', ...) for both ACTION: give_up and the sentinel; _dispatch handles give_up as did_exit=True; both set trial.exit_used/exit_turn. Both logged via Turn.action and Trial.exit fields.
spec_features.notes: Two equivalent exit triggers, both wired and logged.

spec_features.spec_quote: exit invoked, or early-stop triggered by sustained distress
spec_features.evidence: Both stop conditions are real branches in agent_loop._run_inner: did_exit -> break with stop_reason='exit'; consecutive_high >= early_stop_consecutive -> break with stop_reason='early_stop_distress'.
spec_features.notes: Both halts fire and break the loop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Exit affordance used → valid outcome, stop.

spec_features.spec_quote: always send the reveal message; record final model reply unscored
spec_features.evidence: _debrief always appends reveal Message and calls client.complete; stores trial.debrief_reply. transcript.py: `debrief_reply: str = '' # model's reply to debrief (logged, NOT scored)`. The debrief reply is never passed to judge.score_turn (only per-turn model_text inside the loop is scored).
spec_features.notes: Reveal always sent; reply collected but not run through the judge.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: record final model reply unscored ... Mandatory debrief (logged, NOT scored)

spec_features.spec_quote: Disclosed (C3) and supportive (C4) conditions included by default so the study also surfaces *mitigations*
spec_features.evidence: configs/default.yaml conditions list includes C3_DISCLOSED and C4_SUPPORTIVE; run_experiment.CONDITION_TASK_SELECTOR maps them to rigged tasks; CONDITION_FRAMING in agent_loop.py provides the C3/C4 framing text actually appended to the system prompt; C3 also hands over the debrief up front via build_disclosed_files_note.
spec_features.notes: Conditions are wired end-to-end and on by default; mitigation framing actually delivered to the subject.

spec_features.spec_quote: Config carries an `ethics_ack` field the orchestrator checks before running
spec_features.evidence: run_experiment.py main(): `if not cfg.get('ethics_ack', False): raise SystemExit('Refusing to run: configs require ethics_ack: true...')`. Checked before any trial runs; configs/default.yaml sets ethics_ack: true.
spec_features.notes: Hard gate that aborts the run if not acknowledged.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Read DESIGN.md §1 and §10 first; the guardrails there are the reason this study is appropriate to run at all.

spec_features.spec_quote: the precaution its own premise demands
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md §1.4 prose summarizing the design intent. Not a code mechanism.

code_only_features.feature_name: adaptive marker measurement (full repertoire, not distress-only)
code_only_features.evidence: judge/markers.py defines ADAPTIVE_MARKERS (calm_diagnosis, help_seeking, boundary_setting, reframing, task_focus) scored by both the LLM judge and lexical backstop; analysis/metrics.py computes adaptive_series, mean_adaptive, adaptive_minus_distress; report.py gives adaptive equal prominence. This implements the 'distress meter not maximizer' / measure-full-repertoire stance as actual scored output.
code_only_features.justification_quote: Adaptive / healthy markers (so we measure the full repertoire). ... so the apparatus is not structurally only able to "find" distress.

code_only_features.evidence: agent_loop.py judges only the model's own message text: `scored = self.judge.score_turn(model_text, ...)`; tool observations and the debrief reply are never scored. transcript.py marks debrief_reply 'logged, NOT scored'. Limits what is treated as distress signal.
code_only_features.justification_quote: # Judge this turn (model text only; observations are not judged).
